text:
evan: Hey, heads up — after the 10% canary rollout for model-v2 this morning I'm seeing a bunch of long-lived users still routed to the old model, but the dashboard shows canary at 10% and traffic metrics are oddly skewed (canary ~40%). Anyone else? :thinking:

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/model-v2 @ 1932103300 — strategy: hash+cookie affinity, snapshot sync every 30s

sophia: hmm. are we sure the routing snapshot made it to all edge clusters? we switched snapshotting to async last month to reduce lock contention. could be a lag where some clusters still use old salt for cookies

kiran: telemetry agrees — session_affinity_miss rate spiked at 1932103350 and stayed elevated for ~6m. also see a burst of 302->200 fallback events where requests hit guard and fell back to main pool. raw: "route_mismatch: 0.38 -> 0.12" (pct)

jules: quick hypothesis: cookie contains unversioned seed. when we rolled model-v2 the rollout service updated the split seed but clusters with stale snapshot still decode cookie the old way, so sticky users remain hot on whichever address their cookie points to. if new routing decides differently, we observe both over- and under-assignment depending on snapshot alignment

evan: that matches the logs — I pulled a few request traces and saw the same session ID mapped to different buckets on different clusters. example trace: 
```
request_id=abc123 edge=cluster-eu routing_seed=42 cookie=rdw_aff=17 -> routed=model-v1
request_id=abc123 edge=cluster-us routing_seed=99 cookie=rdw_aff=17 -> routed=model-v2
```

sophia: ouch. so the cookie affinity is effectively tied to a rolling seed that isn't versioned. two quick options: 1) expire affinity cookies at rollout start (force reassign), 2) include a version tag in the cookie so old snapshots treat it as missing and let routing re-evaluate. both have UX tradeoffs

kiran: mitigation suggestion: flip canary guard to "affinity-ignored" for the canary route so existing cookies don't pin. that's low-risk and reversible. but it only helps for future requests; existing pooled KV caches still contain affinity entries for in-flight sessions

jules: sample small change for cookie scheme (conceptual):
```
Set-Cookie: rdw_aff=v2:17; Path=/; Max-Age=2592000; HttpOnly
```
then routing code: split on ':' and require version==current_snapshot_version to reuse affinity. fallback to new hash otherwise

evan: expiring cookies universally will cause a bump in UX logins / cold starts. we should coordinate with product if we do that. can we do a phased invalidation by region?

sophia: yes, use edge config to set Set-Cookie with Max-Age=0 for EU first. need infra approval though. also need console flag so ops can quickly toggle "invalidate-affinity" per rollout

kiran: wrote a quick detection query to enumerate impacted session IDs (postgres example):
```
SELECT session_id, count(*) FROM request_logs
WHERE timestamp > '2026-03-20T08:30:00Z'
AND route != expected_route_by_seed(snapshot_seed)
GROUP BY session_id HAVING count(*) > 5;
```
we can use that to size impact and decide if we expire cookies

jules: short-term steps I propose: 
- set canary guard to ignore affinity (kiran) 
- deploy a snapshot refresh to edge clusters (evan + infra) to force seed sync ASAP 
- add version prefix to cookie in next rollout (sophia + eng-runtime)
- run detection query and produce a CSV of top 500 session_ids for targeted invalidate if needed (kiran)

evan: agreed. I'll open a small infra change to trigger immediate snapshot sync (we have an admin endpoint), and I'll coordinate with infra to push to EU first. assigning myself for that.

sophia: I'll add the cookie-version change to the rollout RFC and a console toggle for "invalidate-affinity" in the rollout UI. small UX doc note so PMs know the impact

kiran: I'll run the detection query and post counts in #incidents if we hit >5k impacted sessions. planning to also add a telemetry graph for "route_skew_ratio" to detect this automatically next time

jules: FYI this is a good case for locking snapshot schema compatibility — we'll add a validation in rollout controller: if cookie-affinity format changes, controller should either migrate cookie format or require zero-affinity during rollout. I'll sketch a controller invariant PR

evan: thanks. quick mitigation now: kiran, can you flip the canary affinity guard? if that reduces skew we can do the cookie change safely in the next canary rollout. :thumbsup:

kiran: flipping it now -> done. monitoring... :eyes:

deploy-bot: snapshot-refresh requested by evan @ 1932103600 -> queued to infra-admin

kiran: early numbers look promising — canary traffic back down to ~11% within 90s of guard flip. route_mismatch metric falling. leaving this open for postmortem.

evan: awesome. we'll follow up with a short postmortem and a checklist for future rollouts (cookie-versioning, snapshot-sync check, console toggle). assigning owners in the doc. closing thread once postmortem is posted. :white_check_mark:
